composing_units: 30th Infantry Division (from noon 28 July); Combat Command A, 2nd Armored Division, with the 22nd Infantry attached (temporary, from noon 28 July); 113th Cavalry Group (from noon 28 July); 29th and 28th Infantry Divisions (displacing into the zone, control not dated)
current_activity: displacing west of the Vire and taking over the 30th Division and CCA, 2nd Armored
notes: Event date: Breakout-15 p285 (evening of 27 July Bradley decided to displace XIX Corps west of the Vire; the 35th Division went to V Corps) and p296 (at noon on 28 July Corlett assumed responsibility for the units already engaged in his new zone: the 30th Division, CCA of the 2nd Armored Division reinforced by the 4th Division's 22nd Infantry, and the 113th Cavalry Group); Breakout-16 p304 (the 30th Division and CCA had been transferred from VII to XIX Corps by 28 July). Event definition: XIX Corps changes from the Vire sector east of the river to the zone west of it. The listed formations did not all come under the corps at one moment: three units from noon 28 July, the 28th and 29th Divisions displacing into the zone that day with no control date given. CCA is a separate temporary component (C0515): XIX Corps controlled CCA, not the whole 2nd Armored Division, which stayed with VII Corps until early August (C0507, C0226). composing_units therefore lists dated, qualified entries and is not an organic order of battle. Location: the CMH command-post list has the corps at Saint-Lô on 30 July, two days later. Relationship: First Army assigned; the transfer of the units is 'transferred' in the sources, not stated as assigned or attached, so their rows keep the table relationship. Event support: high (Green Book, noon 28 July). Location support: low (command post listed two days later).

current_activity: command post at Tourouvre as the corps assembles for the Seine drive
notes: Event date: Breakout-28 p576: pinched out of the Argentan-Falaise pocket, XIX Corps displaced more than a hundred miles from Flers/Gacé to the Dreux gap and by 19 August was concentrated with the 2nd Armored, 28th and 30th Divisions in the Mortagne-Brezolles area. Event definition: corps headquarters and divisions assemble for the drive to the Seine. Location: the CMH command-post list gives Tourouvre on 19 August (between Mortagne and Brezolles); commune centroid. Relationship: First Army assigned.

current_activity: attacking toward Elbeuf with 2nd Armored and 30th Divisions abreast
notes: Event date: Breakout-28 p578: on 20 August XIX Corps attacked with the 2nd Armored on the left (Verneuil-Elbeuf axis) and the 30th on the right (Nonancourt to Autheuil), the 28th echeloned left rear; 2nd Armored spearheads reached the southern outskirts of Elbeuf by 24 August. composing_units: 79th Infantry Division; 30th Infantry Division; 2nd Armored Division
current_activity: taking command of 79th, 30th and 2nd Armored Divisions in the Mantes bridgehead
notes: Event date: Breakout-31 p672: at noon on 29 August, as XV Corps headquarters started for an assembly area southeast of Paris, Corlett's XIX Corps took command of the three divisions east of the Seine and moved 2nd Armored Division to the lead. Event definition: XIX Corps takes command of the 79th, 30th and 2nd Armored Divisions, all effective 29 August (the divisions' own rows carry the matching corps entries). Location: the bridgehead area is the corps sector, not the corps command post, which is not located in the sources used (the earlier point was a front-line point at Mantes). Relationship: XIX Corps assigned to First Army. Batch 2: the corps command post that day was at Les Mureaux (C0496, CMH list via World War II by Day); this row keeps the bridgehead sector because the event is the takeover of the three divisions. The 2nd Armored sequence under XIX / XV / XIX Corps (19, 28, 29 August) is modelled in C0229 and the new rows C0509-C0511; the table date 19 August and the narrative date 29 August describe different events, not one. Batch 2 review: the XV Corps command of the 2nd Armored on 28 August is temporary operational control (C0510).

current_activity: command post at Les Mureaux as the corps takes over the Mantes bridgehead
notes: Event date: 29 August 1944 (CMH command-post list as compiled by World War II by Day: Septeuil 28 August, Les Mureaux 29 August); Breakout-31 p672 has the corps taking command of the Mantes bridgehead divisions at noon that day (C0333). Event definition: headquarters location only; the command change is C0333, whose point is the bridgehead sector. Location: Les Mureaux commune centroid, just east of Mantes-Gassicourt. Relationship: First Army assigned.

current_activity: driving from the Albert Canal toward the West Wall
notes: Siegfried-5 p97 maps the XIX Corps drive from the Albert Canal to the West Wall for 10–19 September; on 16 September a task force crossed the Maastricht Canal north of Maastricht (p112).

current_activity: 30th Division links with 1st Division at Würselen, closing the Aachen ring
notes: Event date: 16 October 1944 (Siegfried p305: at 1544 on 16 October the 1st Division chief of staff reported troops of the 18th Infantry on Ravels Hill seeing the 30th Division men at Würselen; p312: the juncture closed the Würselen gap in the Aachen encirclement). Event definition: XIX Corps is credited with the northern arm of the encirclement of Aachen: its 30th Division, after piercing the West Wall near Palenberg, meets VII Corps' 1st Division. The row is about the link-up, not the later surrender (see the VII Corps row of 21 October). Relationship: First Army assigned (the corps passes to Ninth Army on 22 October, see that row). Location: Corps command post at Heerlen from 13 October (atlas); no move is recorded for 16 October, so the nearest earlier entry is used. Coordinates: Wikipedia (en): Heerlen. Event support: high (a timed telephone call in the Green Book). Location support: moderate (atlas list entry three days before; the corps place is a town centroid). Commander: the Green Book names McLain as the XIX Corps commander (p401, p499).

notes: Event date: 16 November 1944 (Siegfried p499: McLain telephoned the code words to Hobbs to show the attack was on; p523: D Day, 16 November, with the 2d Armored and 29th Divisions moving soon after midnight).
